target_customer: Small shop owners and micro-businesses in India with daily income, and lenders who collect daily
problem: Borrowers earn daily but repay monthly, causing cash gaps and defaults; daily auto-debit repayments smooth this.
business_model: Lending marketplace earning commissions from banks and NBFCs (current model)

founders.name: Saurabh Gupta
founders.background_notes: Spent two years at FinBox building lending-tech products.

competitors.name: BharatPe
competitors.what: Merchant payments and loans with daily repayment via daily settlements

competitors.name: Indifi
competitors.what: SME lender with repayment linked to daily card and digital receipts

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace with wallet auto-debit mandates and lender integrations was standard fintech engineering inside RBI rules.

defensibility.rationale: Daily repayment data could give lenders early default signals, but lenders and payment players already collected daily settlements.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Payment players already offered daily-repayment loans; ClickPe moved toward a broader loans, cards and savings marketplace.

market_need_then: Daily-income merchants repay monthly loans, with pain visible in the YC launch post; India had many daily repayment lenders by 2022, indicating real demand.

branding.name_origin: Formerly DailyPe, referring to daily payment; ClickPe's origin not stated in sources.
branding.domain_note: Now uses clickpe.ai; earlier YC profile linked to dailype.

identity.voice_and_tone: Simple taglines: 'Finance on a Click', later 'All Your Finances. One Click.'

brand_strength.rationale: No independent press on the brand; rename dropped the daily-repayment angle as the marketplace broadened.

pivots.from: Daily repayment business loans for shop owners (DailyPe)
pivots.to: General financial marketplace for loans, cards and savings accounts
pivots.why: Not stated by sources; inferred from current site positioning

outcome_analysis: ClickPe began as DailyPe, a daily repayment loan marketplace for shop owners, and joined YC in Winter 2023. It remains active and now markets a wider loans, cards and savings marketplace through regulated lenders; one aggregator claims about $2M revenue by September 2025, which is unverified. No shutdown, layoffs or acquisition were found. Confidence in success factors is limited.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators claim $500K from Y Combinator in 2023 and Inc42 lists the company as bootstrapped with a different founder name (Akhil Nair); no rounds recorded. Revenue and headcount claims are from aggregators. Pivot and rebrand dates are approximate. Outcome search returned only unrelated lenders. strong_pmf is weakly supported. Completeness pass: Round added: the 500K from Y Combinator in 2023 rests on a single weak aggregator (geo.sig.ai, described there as seed); no press found in a second search. It may simply be YC's standard deal.
